question: Find the average of odd numbers from 48 to 350.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The average of any uniformly spaced sequence (like consecutive odd numbers) is simply the average of its first and last terms.

First odd number after 48 = 49

Last odd number before 350 = 349

Average = (49 + 349) ÷ 2 = 398 ÷ 2 = 199

**∴ The correct answer is 199.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2

**Given:**

The sequence of numbers strictly ranges from 48 to 350.

**Formula Used:**

Average of an Arithmetic Progression (AP) = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

The sequence of odd numbers between 48 and 350 forms an Arithmetic Progression: 49, 51, 53, ..., 349

⇒ First odd number (a) = 49

⇒ Last odd number (l) = 349

⇒ Average = (49 + 349) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 398 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 199

**∴ The correct answer is 199.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of First n Odd Numbers

The average of the first n odd natural numbers is exactly n.

Average of First n Even Numbers

The average of the first n even natural numbers is always (n + 1).

Average of an Arithmetic Progression

For any sequence forming an AP, the average is the mean of its first and last terms: (a + l) ÷ 2.

Number of Terms in an AP

The total number of terms n can be found using the formula: n = [(Last term − First term) ÷ Common Difference] + 1.
